purpose: Heavy Rebuild v2 clean-master architectural and process program for the authoritative ruined grain elevator asset, preserving a legible bulk-grain receiving, vertical handling, storage and dispatch complex with structurally supported bins, headhouse equipment, service circulation, dust-control features, terrain seating and coherent damage behavior.
ground_program: truck or wagon receiving approach provides a believable road connection, queueing and turning path into a protected unloading pit without forcing vehicles through occupied building space

receiving pit, hopper and conveyor or bucket-elevator intake form a continuous material path from delivered grain into the vertical handling system rather than acting as disconnected decorative machinery
silo or bin foundations visibly carry the mass of the storage cells into the ground and maintain plausible separation from vehicle lanes, doors and occupied service spaces
dispatch loading area connects stored grain back to truck, rail or other bulk transport through a credible spout, conveyor or hopper arrangement with sufficient vehicle clearance
operator office, scale or control position has sight or instrument access to receiving and dispatch operations and includes a plausible staff entrance and basic service space
electrical, motor, gearbox and transfer equipment is grouped in reachable service zones rather than hidden inside inaccessible solid masses
dust collection, venting, fire separation and explosion-relief logic is represented where enclosed grain handling would otherwise create an implausibly hazardous sealed volume
service yard, drainage, retaining features, hardstand and slab transitions seat the elevator into surrounding terrain without floating foundations, buried doors or disconnected transport elevations
upper_program: headhouse or gallery contains the upper conveyor, distributor and bucket-elevator discharge relationships needed to route grain into individual storage bins
bin tops, catwalks and service galleries use supported beams, guard relationships and maintenance clearances rather than unsupported decorative bridges
vertical service circulation reaches the headhouse, gallery and principal equipment levels by enclosed stair or a combination of stair and equipment-only ladder appropriate to occupancy
roof vents, dust-control equipment, spouting and transfer machinery remain structurally supported and accessible for maintenance
elevated loading spouts or conveyor bridges maintain believable support frames and clearance over road or rail paths
circulation: bulk-delivery vehicles can approach, unload and leave without an unavoidable conflict with dispatch traffic or staff entrances
dispatch vehicles can align beneath loading equipment and exit without clipping structural supports or requiring impossible turning radii
staff circulation connects office or control space, receiving equipment, vertical circulation, headhouse and dispatch systems without requiring routine travel through active grain pits
maintenance circulation reaches motors, bearings, conveyors, elevator legs, bin-top equipment, dust-control systems and electrical equipment
guarded platforms and catwalks provide usable access around elevated machinery while ladders remain restricted to equipment-service roles
emergency egress from occupied upper levels remains legible and does not depend on a single exposed ladder adjacent to hazardous machinery
damage_constraints: the ruined derivative must remain immediately recognizable as a grain elevator through surviving silo or bin massing, receiving geometry, headhouse or conveyor relationships and bulk-loading infrastructure
favor localized bin-wall failure, conveyor collapse, roof or headhouse damage, vehicle impact, corrosion, fire, grain spill and vegetation intrusion over uniform random deletion
collapsed elevated conveyors, galleries or loading spouts must fail from identifiable supports and resolve attached machinery, railings and roof sections so floating fragments are not left behind
silo damage may breach one or more cells and expose internal grain or structural surfaces but should preserve enough intact storage geometry to communicate the former bulk-handling function
receiving and dispatch damage should retain at least one legible material-flow relationship from intake through vertical handling or storage to loading
occupied service spaces must retain at least one viable exploration and egress path after damage unless a deliberately sealed hazard variant is explicitly authored
terrain, hardstand, drainage and transport interfaces should remain coherent after damage rather than becoming disconnected pads or arbitrary pits
derive damaged, occupied or contaminated variants only from this immutable clean master

production_admission.note: Approval state is reconciled to the pre-existing authoritative entry in dev/structure_library/production-approvals.json. This program file does not create a new approval or claim additional validator evidence beyond what the registry records.
